citeAs: Xinhao Li, Yi Wang, Jiashuo Yu, Xiangyu Zeng, Yuhan Zhu, Haian Huang, Jianfei Gao, Kunchang Li, Yinan He, Chenting Wang, Yu Qiao, Yali Wang, Limin Wang (2025). VideoChat-Flash: Hierarchical Compression for Long-Context Video Modeling. arXiv:2501.00574.
creator: Xinhao Li, Yi Wang, Jiashuo Yu, Xiangyu Zeng, Yuhan Zhu, Haian Huang, Jianfei Gao, Kunchang Li, Yinan He, Chenting Wang, Yu Qiao, Yali Wang, Limin Wang (Shanghai AI Laboratory, Nanjing University, Shenzhen Institutes of Advanced Technology CAS)
description: A large-scale long video instruction-tuning dataset named LongVid, comprising 114,228 long videos and 3,444,849 question-answering (QA) pairs across five different task types (video captioning, temporal grounding, event relation recognition, scene relation recognition, and video event counting). The dataset is curated from Ego4D, HowTo100M, HD-VILA, and MiraData, and is used as part of the multi-stage short-to-long training scheme for VideoChat-Flash.
name: VideoChat-Flash Training Data (LongVid)
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Dense event labels are generated for each long video by leveraging existing high-quality short video captions. For datasets with high-quality event-level annotations (HT-Step for HowTo100M, Ego4D-HCap for Ego4D), these are used directly as event labels. For others (MiraData, HD-VILA), major events are extracted from captions using an LLM. QA pairs are then constructed based on video captions, event labels, and timestamps of short video segments across five task types: video captioning, temporal grounding, event relation recognition, scene relation recognition, and video event counting.
rai:dataCollection: LongVid is curated from four open-source video datasets: Ego4D (3,662 egocentric long videos), HowTo100M (how-to videos using HowToInterlink7M captions and HTStep annotations), HD-VILA (in-the-wild videos filtered for segments reconstructable into >60s long videos from the 10M training subset), and MiraData (minute-level movie segments with multi-level captions). Dense event labels are generated for each long video using existing high-quality short video captions and event-level annotations. QA pairs are constructed based on video captions, event labels, and timestamps.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw source data includes videos from Ego4D (egocentric videos), HowTo100M (instructional how-to videos), HD-VILA (high-resolution in-the-wild videos), and MiraData (large-scale movie segments). Corresponding captions come from Panda-70M (for HD-VILA), CosMo/HowToInterlink7M (for HowTo100M), Ego4D-HCap (for Ego4D), and original MiraData captions.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Web Scraping
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Consecutive video segments from source datasets are regrouped/filtered to form long video sequences (>60s). For HD-VILA, consecutive segments are filtered and reconstructed into long videos. Captions at different granularities are merged (e.g., short captions concatenated to form dense medium/long captions for Ego4D). Five types of QA pairs are synthetically constructed from captions, event labels, and timestamps.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For each source dataset: (1) Ego4D: Ego4DHcap hierarchical captions used directly; short captions merged to form dense medium/long captions. (2) MiraData: event and background labels extracted from captions using Qwen-72b LLM. (3) HowTo100M: HowToInterlink7M captions used; HTStep annotations used for event/temporal tasks. (4) HD-VILA: consecutive video segments filtered to reconstruct videos >60s from the 10M training subset; event labels extracted from Panda-70M captions using an LLM. Five task types of QA pairs are constructed: video captioning, temporal grounding, event relation recognition, scene relation recognition, and video event counting.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset enables MLLMs to process long-form video content such as movies, documentaries, surveillance videos, and online video streams, which has broad societal applications including anomaly detection in surveillance, movie understanding, and instructional video comprehension.
rai:dataUseCases: Training multimodal large language models (MLLMs) for long video understanding, including tasks such as video captioning, temporal grounding, event relation recognition, scene relation recognition, and video event counting. Specifically designed for the short-to-long learning scheme to enable models to handle videos of varying lengths (from short clips to hour-long videos).
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Qwen-72b LLM (used to extract event and background labels from captions for MiraData and HD-VILA); VideoChat2 (used to recaption WebVid2M video descriptions); Gemini (used to recaption WebVid and Kinetics videos for detailed descriptions); LLaVA-NeXT-34B (used to recaption images for detailed image descriptions in Stage 2 pre-training).
